newsitem.title: CANADA: Newbridge shares turn positive on earnings.
newsitem.headline: Newbridge shares turn positive on earnings.

text.p: Newbridge Networks Corp shares turned positive mid-morning on the Toronto and New York exchanges on Wednesday after falling at the open.
Newbridge stock tracked a fairly wide range. On the Toronto Stock Exchange, it traded as low as 44.55 and as high as 46.55. It was up 0.45 at 45.95 late morning.
In New York, the shares were 1/2 higher at 34-1/8 after ranging between 34-1/4 and 32-7/8.
The stock's reaction both before and after Tuesday's earnings release was more muted than it has been in previous quarters, Dillon Read analyst Robert MacLellan said.
"I think what you are seeing is a return to more rational decision-making when it comes to Newbridge as a stock," MacLellan said.
"What's happened in the past, up until this quarter, was wild speculation about the quarter which caused the stock to fluctuate five, 10 or 15 percent. That didn't happen this time," he added.
Analysts said the stock may have sold off initially on Wednesday because the company posted earnings one U.S. cent short of consensus earnings estimates.

Newbridge posted a profit of C$0.36 per share in the fiscal third quarter ending January 26 versus C$0.31 a share in the prior-year period. Under U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, and excluding all extraordinaries, Newbridge earned US$0.27 per share in the quarter.
But the positive story underlying the earnings report led investors to resume buying soon afterward, analysts said.

They cited a solid balance sheet, impressive growth in Newbridge's flagship asynchronous transfer mode technology and frame relay as well as the speed with which newly acquired UB Networks was digested.
"Their earnings were pretty much in line. But the story was really not their earnings here. It was the product mix," Wojtek Uzdelewicz of Cowen & Co said.
"If you look at the packet (switching) business, that's their new story. It's where most of the growth is coming. It grew by 25 percent sequentially," he added.
Uzdelewicz said there were some concerns several quarters ago that Newbridge's frame relay, packet and ATM businesses were threatened by competitors.
"But this quarter shows that far from losing ground, Newbridge is probably gaining market share," he said.
Uzdelewicz said Cowen raised its fiscal 1998 earnings estimate to US$1.45 from US$1.43 a share based on the prospects for packet switching growth.
But the brokerage lowered its fiscal fourth-quarter estimate to US$0.29 from US$0.31 a share, more in line with analysts' estimates.
"If you look at the product mix, there's a good chance that in 1998 we might see a nice acceleration in earnings," Uzdelewicz said.
